_schema: entry_id -> { cat: creature|item|place, title, body, hint }. Logs come from readables.json at runtime.

creature_gull.title: Gulls
creature_gull.body: Still here, wheeling the high iron like nothing ever changed. They leave at dusk, every day, all at once — they know the schedule better than I do.
creature_gull.hint: Follow their lead: when the gulls go, get to the light.

creature_jelly_drifter.title: Jelly Drifters
creature_jelly_drifter.body: After dark the water fills with slow teal bells, pulsing as they turn around the rig. The Bloom, up close. They never touch the legs. Beautiful, honestly.
creature_jelly_drifter.hint: They only surface at night. Whatever they feed on rises then too.

creature_barnacle.title: Lamp Barnacles
creature_barnacle.body: Growths on the legs at the waterline that glow at night — until I get close. They feel me coming through the steel and go dark. Shy light.
creature_barnacle.hint: If the barnacles go dark and I haven't moved… something else is on the steel.

creature_lamp_eel.title: Lamp-Eel
creature_lamp_eel.body: A chain of light swimming figure-eights off the north edge, bright at the head and fading down its length. It keeps exactly the same route. Patrolling? Grazing?
creature_lamp_eel.hint: It surfaces at full dark, north side. Best view from the pontoon or the galley roof.

creature_fiddler_shoal.title: Fiddler Shoal
creature_fiddler_shoal.body: Small quick fish schooling under the wet deck lip. Silver by day — but at dusk they catch a teal glint, like the Bloom is getting into them. They vanish at night.
creature_fiddler_shoal.hint: They hide when night comes. Smart fish. Consider imitating the fish.

creature_mantle_ray.title: The Mantle
creature_mantle_ray.body: Something enormous crossed over the rig in the dark — wide flat wings, underside speckled with Bloom-light, a call like a hull groaning. It didn't circle. It was going somewhere.
creature_mantle_ray.hint: The chalk tally on the bunkhouse roof counts something. I think it counts this.

creature_tide_worm.title: Tide Worms
creature_tide_worm.body: Finger-length worms that rise from the deck drains at dawn and dusk, teal-tipped, swaying. Footsteps send them back down. Harmless. I think the word is 'harmless'.
creature_tide_worm.hint: They keep tide hours: dawn and dusk only.

creature_lamplight_crab.title: The Giant Crab
creature_lamplight_crab.body: Dog-sized, blue-shelled, claws like bolt cutters held high. By day they cling below the waterline — lean over the east rim and you can watch them sidle along the pontoon faces. After dark they come up over the deck edge and walk the plate like they own it. They will not cross powered light, and a beam held on one sends it straight back over the rim. In the dark, though, that claw takes a piece of you.
creature_lamplight_crab.hint: Daylight: look over the east deck edge. Night: keep to the lit decks, keep a torch in hand, and if one closes — run; they quit a chase you outrun.

creature_glow_worm.title: Glow Worms
creature_glow_worm.body: A knuckle of teal light in the dark corners — under the stair, against the leg bases. Never the same corners twice. It feels footsteps through the plate and sinks back into its den before I'm anywhere near. Went in low and slow tonight and got a hand around one. Mostly light and muscle.
creature_glow_worm.hint: Crouch to close the last few meters. Sear it at the bench before eating — raw ones bite back.

creature_epic_whale.title: The Four-Eyed
creature_epic_whale.body: It came over the rig higher than the mast — a body like a hull, too many fins all rowing out of time, four eyes burning teal down its back. Swimming the night air the way the sea swims. I didn't hide. It wasn't looking at me. I don't think I register at all.
creature_epic_whale.hint: Full dark, high up, rare. When the long groan comes and the crab isn't moving — look up.

item_canned_food.title: Canned Food
item_canned_food.body: Meridian mess-hall stock. Dented, unlabeled, edible.
item_canned_food.hint: Eat from the hotbar (1–4). Restores a good meal's worth of hunger.

item_canned_peaches.title: Canned Peaches
item_canned_peaches.body: Someone was hoarding these. I understand completely.
item_canned_peaches.hint: Eat from the hotbar. Lighter than a full can of stew.

item_water_ration.title: Water Ration
item_water_ration.body: SPHL survival stock, foil pouch, tastes like the bag.

item_sealed_tin.title: Sealed Tin
item_sealed_tin.body: Fished out of the gyre still watertight. The sea kept it cold.
item_sealed_tin.hint: Eat from the hotbar. The gyre keeps bringing them — keep the hook handy.

item_kelp_bundle.title: Kelp Bundle
item_kelp_bundle.body: Bloom-touched kelp, faintly glowing. The old crew's notes say it's safe. The old crew is gone. It IS safe — probably.
item_kelp_bundle.hint: Edible, small — or bench it: 2× kelp + scrap → bloom lamp. Light the crab honors.

item_cable_spool.title: Cable Spool
item_cable_spool.body: Marine-grade cable, enough to splice a burned run.
item_cable_spool.hint: Take it to the burned cable gap in Breaker Room 4-A, then throw the breaker.

item_prybar.title: Prybar
item_prybar.body: Bent iron, honest tool. The pump room gave it up without a fight.
item_prybar.hint: Craftable: lash it to a rope coil at the rigging bench → throwing hook.

item_rope.title: Rope Coil
item_rope.body: Salt-stiff but sound. The riggers trusted their lives to this stuff.
item_rope.hint: Craftable: rope + prybar at the wet-deck rigging bench → throwing hook.

item_throwing_hook.title: Throwing Hook
item_throwing_hook.body: A heaving line with teeth. The gyre holds what the sea took; this takes it back.
item_throwing_hook.hint: Press F to throw. It combs the surface on the way back — aim past what you want.

item_flare.title: Flare
item_flare.body: Emergency flare, dry. One loud red argument against the dark.
item_flare.hint: No striker yet. There'll be a use for this. (v0.2)

item_life_ring.title: Life Ring
item_life_ring.body: Cork and canvas, 'RIG 4 — SLIPWAY' stenciled almost gone.
item_life_ring.hint: If something goes in the water that shouldn't… this is the answer. (v0.2)

item_driftwood.title: Driftwood Plank
item_driftwood.body: Ship-cut lumber, sea-worn smooth. Not from this rig. From somewhere down the line.
item_driftwood.hint: Bench recipes: 2× driftwood → walkway · with tarp → lean-to · with scrap → barricade.

item_scrap_metal.title: Scrap Metal
item_scrap_metal.body: Plate fragments, still painted on one side. The paint matches this rig's rails.
item_scrap_metal.hint: Bench recipes: with 2× kelp → bloom lamp · 2× scrap + driftwood → barricade.

item_tarp.title: Canvas Tarp
item_tarp.body: Heavy weather canvas, whole and hemmed. A small roof, folded.
item_tarp.hint: Bench recipe: tarp + 2× driftwood → lean-to. A pocket of warmth anywhere.

place_sphl.title: The SPHL
place_sphl.body: Six days sealed in an orange pressure pod while the machine gave my blood back to the surface. It kept me alive and never said a word. The hatch is open now. It stays my bed.
place_sphl.hint: If the night goes wrong, I wake up here. It counts as 'going wrong'.

place_gyre.title: The Gyre
place_gyre.body: The current south of the rig turns in a slow circle, and everything the sea carries ends up turning with it — wood, rope, tins, kelp. At night the Bloom gathers under the eye like it's reading the same current.
place_gyre.hint: Everything spirals to the middle. A thrown hook crosses the whole eye on the reel-in.

place_rigging_bench.title: The Rigging Bench
place_rigging_bench.body: A work-worn bench on the wet deck. Lay parts on its surface and they tell you what they want to become — then you hold the work and hammer it real.
place_rigging_bench.hint: Known so far: throwing hook, bloom lamp, lean-to, walkway, barricade. New parts may know new shapes.

place_fire_barrel.title: The Fire Barrel
place_fire_barrel.body: A drum of coals on the wet deck that someone kept burning. I keep it burning now. Warmth that doesn't need the grid.
place_fire_barrel.hint: Stand close to drive the cold out — the sea soaks into your bones down here.

place_power.title: The Grid
place_power.body: Spliced the burned run, threw Master 4-A, and the floodlights came up with a hum that felt like the rig taking a breath. Light is safety I make.
place_power.hint: The circuit holds the topside floodlights. What walks at night won't cross their wash.

item_bloom_lamp_kit.title: Bloom Lamp (kit)
item_bloom_lamp_kit.body: Kelp sealed in a scrap housing, ready to raise. Cold teal light that needs no breaker, no cable, no grid. Light is safety I make — this is that, portable.
item_bloom_lamp_kit.hint: Press B to build. Place them along the paths you'll need after dark. The crab honors their light.

item_leanto_kit.title: Lean-To (kit)
item_leanto_kit.body: Canvas over driftwood, folded flat and lashed for carrying.
item_leanto_kit.hint: Press B to build. A pocket of warmth anywhere on the rig — no grid required.

item_walkway_kit.title: Plank Walkway (kit)
item_walkway_kit.body: A lashed plank section. The rig ends where its decks end — unless I say otherwise.
item_walkway_kit.hint: Press B to build. Bridges gaps, extends decks, makes paths.

item_barricade_kit.title: Barricade (kit)
item_barricade_kit.body: Scrap plate on a wood brace. Waist-high and stubborn.
item_barricade_kit.hint: Press B to build. Cover, wind-break, or just a wall where I want a wall.

place_building.title: Building
place_building.body: I raised something on this rig with my own hands. It wasn't here yesterday; it's here now. The rig doesn't mind. I think the rig has been waiting for someone to keep making things.
place_building.hint: Craft kits at the bench → B for build mode → LMB places, R rotates, Tab cycles kits.

creature_seal.title: Harbor Seal
creature_seal.body: One hauled out on the wet deck this morning and watched me the whole time I worked. No fear in it at all — the Bloom took that from all of them. When I looked back, it looked back. Twelve years ago they'd have bolted. Now I think it was deciding about me.
creature_seal.hint: They herd fish toward a still net. Earn one's trust and you never fish alone.

creature_lamp_snail.title: Lamp Snails
creature_lamp_snail.body: Lean over the rail on a dark night and the legs are wearing lamps — shells the size of a wheelbarrow with cold light running through them in veins, the way light runs through alabaster held up to a window. They drift slow circles at the waterline and the whole rig stands in that glow after sundown.
creature_lamp_snail.hint: On an outgoing tide some strand on the leg bracing. A gentle harvest takes the glow-mucus and leaves the animal.

creature_corvid_gull.title: Corvid-Gull
creature_corvid_gull.body: This one didn't wheel off with the others. It sat the rail and tipped its head, tracking me with one bright eye — measuring. They steal anything loose and bright, and they remember faces. I get the feeling the trade could go both ways, if I'm patient.
creature_corvid_gull.hint: Leave something shiny where one perches. Their taste is inscrutable, but they pay.

fish_herring.title: Lantern Herring
fish_herring.body: The shoal glows. You can net them at night by their own light — the sea's little mercy.
fish_herring.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_slate_cod.title: Slate Cod
fish_slate_cod.body: Heavy, slow, scales like roofing slate. It fought like a wet sandbag and I was still glad of it.
fish_slate_cod.hint: Bites: day · storms help · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_mirrorjack.title: Mirrorjack
fish_mirrorjack.body: Chrome flanks — it threw the dawn light back at me so hard I nearly lost the rod.
fish_mirrorjack.hint: Bites: dawn/dusk · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

fish_chimefish.title: Chimefish
fish_chimefish.body: It rang against the rail when I lifted it clear. Rang. Like a struck glass.
fish_chimefish.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · calm seas only · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_sable_hake.title: Sable Hake
fish_sable_hake.body: They rise to worklight after dark like moths with fins. The floodlit rail is a fishing spot now.
fish_sable_hake.hint: Bites: night · close to the rig · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

fish_barrel_grouper.title: Goliath Grouper
fish_barrel_grouper.body: Bloom-big. It feeds a week. My arms will remember this one.
fish_barrel_grouper.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · storms help · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Prime Fillet

fish_ribbon_eel.title: Ribbon Eel
fish_ribbon_eel.body: It came up crackling with faint charge, taste of a storm in the line. The Bloom keeps strange batteries.
fish_ribbon_eel.hint: Bites: night · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Prime Fillet

fish_the_looker.title: The Looker
fish_the_looker.body: I had it at the rail. It looked back at me — considered me — and I opened my hands before I decided to. Some things you release.
fish_the_looker.hint: Ultra-rare. It is never kept. It was never going to be kept.

system_fishing.title: Fishing
system_fishing.body: The rod from the storeroom works. Cast to open water, watch the float, strike when it dips — then it's a conversation: reel when the line slacks, rest when it screams.
system_fishing.hint: Hold LMB to reel, ease off before the tension bar tops out.

system_drop_net.title: The Drop Net
system_drop_net.body: Rope and driftwood and patience. Lower it, walk away, come back to breakfast. The rig fishes for me now.
system_drop_net.hint: Soaks best through dusk and dark.

system_stove.title: The Galley Stove
system_stove.body: The old range still holds pressure in its bottle. Seared fish, hot pan, the galley smelling alive for the first time since the Flash.
system_stove.hint: COOK at the stove turns raw catch into a real meal.

item_fishing_rod.title: Fishing Rod
item_fishing_rod.body: A rigger's rod from the storeroom, cork grip worn to the shape of somebody's hands. The sea is a pantry now — this is the key.
item_fishing_rod.hint: Select it on the hotbar; LMB casts to open water.

item_drop_net_kit.title: Drop Net
item_drop_net_kit.body: Rope, driftwood, patience. The rig can fish while I sleep.
item_drop_net_kit.hint: Place it at a deck edge — it needs open water below.

item_cooked_fish.title: Seared Fish
item_cooked_fish.body: Hot pan, honest meat. The galley smells alive again.
item_cooked_fish.hint: Eat from the hotbar. Beats canned everything.

item_cooked_fish_prime.title: Prime Fillet
item_cooked_fish_prime.body: The big deep ones render down rich. A real meal, the kind you sit down for.
item_cooked_fish_prime.hint: The grouper and the eel sear into this.

item_fish_herring.title: Lantern Herring (raw)
item_fish_herring.body: It glows faintly even out of the water.
item_fish_herring.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

item_fish_slate_cod.title: Slate Cod (raw)
item_fish_slate_cod.body: Heavy as its name. Scales like roof slate.

item_fish_mirrorjack.title: Mirrorjack (raw)
item_fish_mirrorjack.body: Chrome-flanked and fast. Dawn water made solid.

item_fish_chimefish.title: Chimefish (raw)
item_fish_chimefish.body: It rang when it came over the rail.

item_fish_sable_hake.title: Sable Hake (raw)
item_fish_sable_hake.body: Riser to worklight. The floodlit rail fishes best after dark.

item_fish_ribbon_eel.title: Ribbon Eel (raw)
item_fish_ribbon_eel.body: Still faintly crackling. Handle with respect.

fish_copper_sprat.title: Copper Sprat
fish_copper_sprat.body: Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. The sea's small change.
fish_copper_sprat.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_copper_sprat.title: Copper Sprat (raw)
item_fish_copper_sprat.body: Bait-tier shoals that trail anything moving. The sea's small change.
item_fish_copper_sprat.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_silver_ladder.title: Silver Ladder
fish_silver_ladder.body: Dawn columns over open water — the shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar.
fish_silver_ladder.hint: Bites: dawn · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_silver_ladder.title: Silver Ladder (raw)
item_fish_silver_ladder.body: Dawn columns over open water — the shoal stacks vertical, a shimmering pillar.
item_fish_silver_ladder.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_ember_snapper.title: Ember Snapper
fish_ember_snapper.body: Warm-bodied — crowds the rig's outfalls and warm steel. Fish the shadow of the deck.
fish_ember_snapper.hint: Bites: day/dusk · close to the rig · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_ember_snapper.title: Ember Snapper (raw)
item_fish_ember_snapper.body: Warm-bodied — crowds the rig's outfalls and warm steel. Fish the shadow of the deck.

fish_ghost_sole.title: Ghost Sole
fish_ghost_sole.body: Near-invisible by day. Night water near a glow is where it shows itself.
fish_ghost_sole.hint: Bites: night · close to the rig · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_ghost_sole.title: Ghost Sole (raw)
item_fish_ghost_sole.body: Near-invisible by day. Night water near a glow is where it shows itself.
item_fish_ghost_sole.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_glasspike.title: Glasspike
fish_glasspike.body: Clear still nights, open water — a pike you see through, found by the grit in its gut.
fish_glasspike.hint: Bites: night · calm seas only · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_glasspike.title: Glasspike (raw)
item_fish_glasspike.body: Clear still nights, open water — a pike you see through, found by the grit in its gut.
item_fish_glasspike.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_lodestone_bream.title: Lodestone Bream
fish_lodestone_bream.body: Deep daylight water. Its magnetized bones spin a compass — catch enough, craft crude magnets, someday.
fish_lodestone_bream.hint: Bites: day · open water — cast far · takes: rod · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_lodestone_bream.title: Lodestone Bream (raw)
item_fish_lodestone_bream.body: Deep daylight water. Its magnetized bones spin a compass — catch enough, craft crude magnets, someday.

fish_drum_croaker.title: Drum Croaker
fish_drum_croaker.body: Storm fish, full stop. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes — then they bite like they mean it.
fish_drum_croaker.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · storms ONLY · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_drum_croaker.title: Drum Croaker (raw)
item_fish_drum_croaker.body: Storm fish, full stop. You hear the chorus drumming through the hull as the rain comes — then they bite like they mean it.
item_fish_drum_croaker.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_inkwell_squid.title: Inkwell Squid
fish_inkwell_squid.body: Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink — the ink's worth keeping too, someday.
fish_inkwell_squid.hint: Bites: night · drawn to worklight · takes: rod+net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_inkwell_squid.title: Inkwell Squid (raw)
item_fish_inkwell_squid.body: Night jigging. Comes up backwards in a huff of luminous ink — the ink's worth keeping too, someday.
item_fish_inkwell_squid.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_stone_crab.title: Stone Crab
fish_stone_crab.body: Walks into a soaked net, never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard — keep the pieces, someday.
fish_stone_crab.hint: Bites: dusk/night · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_stone_crab.title: Stone Crab (raw)
item_fish_stone_crab.body: Walks into a soaked net, never onto a hook. Shell's ceramic-hard — keep the pieces, someday.
item_fish_stone_crab.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_gutter_prawn.title: Gutter Prawn
fish_gutter_prawn.body: Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few — the pens will want them, someday.
fish_gutter_prawn.hint: Bites: dawn/day/dusk/night · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_gutter_prawn.title: Gutter Prawn (raw)
item_fish_gutter_prawn.body: Net filler. A soak rarely comes up without a few — the pens will want them, someday.
item_fish_gutter_prawn.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_miller_flounder.title: Miller's Flounder
fish_miller_flounder.body: Deck-plate camouflage, bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them by day.
fish_miller_flounder.hint: Bites: day · close to the rig · takes: net · sears to Seared Fish

item_fish_miller_flounder.title: Miller's Flounder (raw)
item_fish_miller_flounder.body: Deck-plate camouflage, bottom habits. Nets working close to the legs find them by day.
item_fish_miller_flounder.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

fish_fathom_halibut.title: Fathom Halibut
fish_fathom_halibut.body: Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up, and the winch knows about it. Feeds a week.
fish_fathom_halibut.hint: Bites: night · takes: net · sears to Prime Fillet

item_fish_fathom_halibut.title: Fathom Halibut (raw)
item_fish_fathom_halibut.body: Door-sized. Only a night-soaked net brings one up, and the winch knows about it. Feeds a week.
item_fish_fathom_halibut.hint: Sear it at the galley stove — raw bites back.

creature_hammerhead.title: Ultra Hammerhead
creature_hammerhead.body: It came off its patrol line the moment I went under — a hammer the width of a doorway swinging through the murk to look at me with both ends of its face. Sometimes it circles. Sometimes it doesn't. I don't get a vote.
creature_hammerhead.hint: They patrol below the swell and mostly attack swimmers who come close. The deck is yours; the water is theirs.

system_preserving.title: Keeping the Catch
system_preserving.body: Raw fish turns in about four hours on the line. The fridge holds it forever. Cooked fish hung up cures into dried fish that keeps — the rig's larder, strung in the wind.
system_preserving.hint: HANG fish on a marked line, or STOW it in the galley fridge. Cooked + 4 hours hung = dried, keeps forever.

item_dried_fish.title: Dried Fish
item_dried_fish.body: Wind-cured on the line. Keeps forever, eats like a hot meal's memory.

item_fish_rotten.title: Rotten Fish
item_fish_rotten.body: Left too long on the line. The gulls won't even argue over it.
item_fish_rotten.hint: Eating this is a mistake you make once.

codex_what_osk_chose.title: What Osk Chose
codex_what_osk_chose.body: Four scraps in four corners of the rig, one man's mind coming apart toward the light instead of the dark. Osk saw it first, on the derrick, the night the water learned his name. He didn't muster. He didn't take a boat. He walked down the line toward the Quiet Rig, toward the thing the company was hiding, because he decided it was worth seeing more than it was worth surviving. I keep his notes in a row now. On the bad nights I'm not sure he was wrong.
codex_what_osk_chose.hint: He kept the lamps lit. So do I. It's the only prayer left that works.

codex_down_the_line.title: Down the Line
codex_down_the_line.body: Food. Cable. Spool stock. Whole pallets, going out on the supply boat, offloaded at night with nobody on deck, all of it flowing toward the platform at the end of the chain — the one they wouldn't name, the one they let the bridges rot toward. A "processing terminus." Nine hundred miles from anywhere, and Meridian was pouring the line's whole throat into its far end. Processing what. I think the honest answer is: they were feeding it. And I think it ate.
codex_down_the_line.hint: The Quiet Rig is seven bridges east. The bridges are gone. Good.

codex_the_flash.title: The Flash
codex_the_flash.body: Every gauge on the drill deck read zero at the same second. The sea lit up under leg four. The toolpusher shut the well in and nobody argued — nobody ever doesn't argue. Then the radios: the water is AWAKE, no code for it, going dark. Whatever the company was growing down the line, it finished growing all at once, and the light came up out of the whole ocean like a held breath let go. They called it the Flash because "the morning the sea opened its eyes" won't fit in a log.
codex_the_flash.hint: It didn't end the world. It woke it. Not the same thing.

codex_the_count.title: The Count
codex_the_count.body: Someone on this rig spent their last good nights up here with a chalk stub, counting the Mantle's crossings. Thirty-one, then a gap where the counting stopped mattering, then four more gouged deep like they were pressing a point into the steel. IT COMES BACK. I've seen it once now. It didn't circle, didn't look down. It was going somewhere on a schedule older than the company. I understand the impulse to keep the tally. It's the only calendar out here that means anything.
codex_the_count.hint: Add your own marks. Something should still be counting.

place_davits.title: The Empty Davits
place_davits.body: Two sets of falls, both run out, both empty. Lifeboat 2 got away. The stencil says it launched full. Somebody stood right here and made the count — forty aboard, one short — and lowered away anyway, because a boat that waits is a boat that drowns. I don't hold it against them. I'd have done the count the same. I'm the number that didn't fit.
place_davits.hint: The falls still work. If anything ever comes back for me, this is where it lands.

place_derrick.title: The Derrick
place_derrick.body: The drill string goes down through the floor and keeps going, past anything I want to think about. The toolpusher's last log said the quiet coming back up it wasn't the quiet of a good hole — it was the quiet of something listening. I stood on the floor at night and put my hand on the pipe. It was warm. Wells aren't warm. I took my hand back.
place_derrick.hint: Osk saw it first from the catwalk up here. Best and worst view on the rig.

place_quiet_rig.title: Platform 7 — The Quiet Rig
place_quiet_rig.body: Seven bridges east, or where they used to be. The end of the line. Where the food went, where the cable went, where the company grew the light and called it a terminus and hoped nobody down the line would count the pallets. I'll never stand on it. The sea took the bridges and won't give a boat leave to go west. Maybe that's the sea keeping me from it. Maybe it's the sea keeping it from me. Either way — thank you.
place_quiet_rig.hint: Everything came from down the line. The Bloom most of all.

creature_rust_snail.title: Rust Snails
creature_rust_snail.body: Follow a bright scoured line in the corrosion far enough and there is an animal at the end of it. Shell the colour of what it eats — oxide orange, banded, flaking — and a warm amber light down in the whorls, the only heat on the whole platform. They rasp the steel. Slowly, patiently, they are taking the rig apart and wearing it.
creature_rust_snail.hint: Where the handrail has gone thin and clean, one has been working. The shell plate is rich in iron if you can get it off.

creature_glass_snail.title: Glass Snails
creature_glass_snail.body: Under the wet-deck lip, on the plate that never sees sun, there is nothing to see but a slow teal spiral turning in the dark. The shell is glass — truly glass — and the light is its gut, working. Come closer and it does not shrink. It burns brighter and turns the lit coil toward you, which is the Bloom all over: curiosity where you expected fear.
creature_glass_snail.hint: They brighten to a nearby lamp. Stand still and the whole underside of the deck lights up.

creature_pyramid_snail.title: Pyramid Snails
creature_pyramid_snail.body: A spire of black and white winding to a point, ringed with pale spikes on every step, riding a broad grey foot that ripples as it goes. It carries its eyes up on stalks and swings them round to hold you while it keeps walking. The other three gastropods never leave the water line. This one crosses the whole topside on its own business, changes its mind about which way is interesting, and goes that way instead.
creature_pyramid_snail.hint: It is going somewhere, not patrolling — wait where you are and it will come to you. Greens will stop it dead, and a fed pair will make a third.

creature_anchor_limpet.title: Anchor Limpets
creature_anchor_limpet.body: A riveted iron cap welded into the splash zone, ringed underneath with a thin band of light. Walk toward one and it feels you through the plate long before you arrive — the shell settles, the ring goes out, and what is left is indistinguishable from the rig. The storm cannot move them. Neither can you.
creature_anchor_limpet.hint: The light only returns if you stop moving. Patience is the whole trick with these.

system_snail_breeding.title: Feeding the Snails
system_snail_breeding.body: Kelp does it. Any lamp, rust or glass snail takes a green offering and glows a shade brighter for it — and once, out on the SW pontoon, I fed two in the same evening and carried one over to sit beside the other. By morning there was a third light, small and pale, working the same patch. Nobody taught them that. They just do it, the way anything alive does it, given enough to eat and something else fed nearby.
system_snail_breeding.hint: FEED a crawling snail a green item. Two fed snails of the same kind, brought within a few metres of each other, breed — a permanent baby, no despawn, ever.

creature_snail_baby.title: A New Light
creature_snail_baby.body: Half the size of its parents and twice as restless, already crawling its own short patch of the leg base. The Bloom's little lights are multiplying because I fed them — not because anyone asked me to keep this rig alive, but I am, one fed snail at a time.
creature_snail_baby.hint: Babies grow to full size over a couple of days. They never starve and they never vanish.

item_snail_live.title: Live Snail
item_snail_live.body: Collected whole — shell, foot, and the last of its light, going out slowly in the dark of the pack. It was crawling a minute ago. I try not to think about which ones I've fed.
item_snail_live.hint: Sears on the galley stove into escargot. Works on a baby the same as a grown one.

item_escargot.title: Escargot
item_escargot.body: Seared in its own shell, small and rich, the first genuinely good meal the rig has given me. It sits fine. I still think about the constellation being one light short tonight, and eat it anyway.
item_escargot.hint: Solid hunger, a little comfort besides — the pot is kinder to you than the tide ever was.

fish_skipjack_tuna.title: Skipjack Tuna
fish_skipjack_tuna.body: The small one, and never alone — skipjack boil the surface in open water by day.

fish_yellowfin_tuna.title: Yellowfin Tuna
fish_yellowfin_tuna.body: Gold down the flank and sickle fins half its own length. Runs when it feels the hook.

fish_albacore_tuna.title: Albacore Tuna
fish_albacore_tuna.body: Pectorals like scythes, reaching most of the way down it. Cold water, long runs.

fish_bigeye_tuna.title: Bigeye Tuna
fish_bigeye_tuna.body: That eye is for the dark water it hunts in. Comes up at dusk, goes down by morning.

fish_bluefin_tuna.title: Bluefin Tuna
fish_bluefin_tuna.body: The big one. A quarter tonne of muscle built like a torpedo — it will empty the spool.

fish_bluelined_grouper.title: Bluelined Grouper
fish_bluelined_grouper.body: Electric blue pinstripes on olive. Holds station in the leg shadow and waits.

fish_peacock_grouper.title: Peacock Grouper
fish_peacock_grouper.body: Covered in blue eyespots, every one ringed black. It watches the whole reef at once.

fish_humpback_grouper.title: Humpback Grouper
fish_humpback_grouper.body: Small head on a steep white back, all over black spots. Odd, slow, unbothered.

fish_leopard_grouper.title: Leopard Coral Grouper
fish_leopard_grouper.body: Coral red, spotted electric blue, and faster off the mark than a fish that size has any right to be.

fish_mahi_mahi.title: Mahi-Mahi
fish_mahi_mahi.body: Green-gold and lit from inside, with a forehead like a blunt axe. Fast, and it jumps.

fish_swallowtail.title: Swallowtail Angelfish
fish_swallowtail.body: Two long tail filaments trailing behind it like a swallow. Barely worth eating; worth looking at.

creature_ship_cat.title: Ship's Cat
creature_ship_cat.body: Somebody's, once. It was washing a paw in the bunkhouse like the evacuation was a rumour. It has decided about me now, and it comes along.
creature_ship_cat.hint: Found in the bunkhouse · say hello once · follows you · settles when you rest · very interested in fish
